rowA.text: Direction A — indigo band, light workspace, amber accent

legend.text: All example content mirrors the deterministic fixtures (project “fixture”, task “Three modules”, items a/b/c, built-in roles). Counts and stages are real backend fields; nothing shows percentages, estimates or model availability that the backend cannot measure. Controls that arrive in U2/U3 are drawn visibly unavailable.

chosen.text: Selected direction: A, with a denser two-column Overview.

rowU3.text: U3 — browser workflows and guided setup (extends Direction A; U1/U2 boards unchanged)

legendU3.text: U3 contracts drawn here: POST /projects with strict ProjectInput and preserved input on failure; one idempotency key per submission attempt, held until the outcome is known; mode/approve/cancel reuse the existing routes and bind to the displayed task version; the diff is read by task identity only, text-only, with unavailable/binary/truncated/empty told apart; setup reuses the terminal flow and never collects credentials or runs a paid test on its own.

rowU4.text: U4 — free disk space, embedded in the existing screens (no new page)

legendU4.text: Contract: GET /tasks/:id/cleanup-preview returns worktrees (path, size, uncommitted and untracked files), branches to delete and keep, run temp data and a digest; POST /tasks/:id/cleanup {digest, savePatch} recomputes ownership and the list and refuses with 409 when anything changed. A completed task's branch is always kept. Events and evidence are never deleted. Nothing is removed automatically.

rowU5.text: U5 — improvements taken from the Paperclip review: liveness rule, answer-only mode, visible cost; compaction added to U4

legendU5.text: Liveness rule: every unfinished task has a live path (engine activity), an explicit waiting path (a decision of yours) or a recovery path (a choice offered to you); anything else is shown as needing attention. Automatic retries are bounded (quota/capacity once, lost dispatch once) and tool calls are never replayed. Costs are provider-reported tokens summed per task and project; prices are optional configuration, never estimates. See docs/IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md.

rowU6.text: U6 — Work tab as a team board: who is finished, who is working, who is left (design only, to be refined together)

legendU6.text: Two treatments on one page: the pipeline (plan → build → review → integrate → commit, with the members who do each stage) and the roster (Finished / Working now / Up next columns). "You" appears as a member whenever a decision is yours. Every value is a recorded run, event or checkpoint; durations are timestamp differences; nothing is estimated. Members the plan does not need are shown as not needed. No new backend field is required. Large teams: each stage and roster column shows up to four full rows; finished members fold into a stack first, then up-next members; working, failed and needs-you rows never fold.

rowU7.text: U7 — GitHub: attach repositories, publish pull requests, address reviews and failed checks (design only; local-only projects unchanged)

legendU7.text: Contract: GitHub is optional per project. One project is one repository: local only (unchanged), a local folder linked to its repository, or a clone DevAgents manages. The account is chosen where a project is added; its token is pasted there the first time, sits in the vault once per account and is shared by that account's projects. Only the service uses it, agents never do. A completed task still ends in a local commit and diff; publishing (push the task branch, open a pull request) is a separate recorded step. Reviews and checks are read by polling. A follow-up round is a normal task that starts from the pull request's latest commit and adds one commit. Per-project policy decides what happens on click or automatically, with a limit on automatic rounds. Never: merge, force-push, push to the default branch. Plan: docs/GITHUB_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md.

rowU8.text: U8 — Integrations per project: Jira is where work comes from, GitHub is where the result goes; either, both or neither (design only)

rowU9.text: U9 — Ticket tools: the only setup a user sees is the seven fields DevAgents reads from a ticket (design only)

legendU9.text: Replaces the long mapping form. A tool is added with name, address and token. DevAgents then reads one real ticket and shows seven rows: ticket number, title and link (to name the ticket and link back), and project, status, assignee and label (to choose which tickets come in). Each row shows the tool's field and the value from that ticket, so a wrong guess is visible. Everything else (which tool lists tickets, where the lists are, fixed arguments) is filled in automatically and folded away. Which project, status, assignee and label to pick is chosen per project, on the project page.

rowU10.text: U10 — Tasks as a board: available tickets, one column per stage, and a separate band for what needs you (design only)

legendU10.text: Needs you is a band above the board, not a column: a decision can be due before planning (mode choice) or after it (plan approval), so those tasks are lifted out of the board to the top, each with one button, and return to the board once decided. The flow below has six columns. Available holds tickets from Jira and the connected ticket tools that match a project's pick-up rule and are not started; a card names its source and ticket number and offers Start task, or says it starts on its own. Then Planning (draft, planning), Queued (ready), Working (running, validating, reviewing, repairing, committing; the chip names the step), Done (completed), Stopped (failed, cancelled). A task that came from a ticket keeps the ticket number on its card. Cards are not dragged. The List view stays behind the Board / List switch. Needs backend work that does not exist yet: reading the matching tickets for Available and starting a task from one. Available has a pin in its top right corner: pinned, it stays open in the row; not pinned, it folds to a narrow strip with its name and count and opens over the board while the mouse is on it. The choice is remembered per browser.

rowU11.text: U11 — Team member: responsibilities in place of the role dropdown, effort, and a model list read from the engine

legendU11.text: The Worker / Planner dropdown becomes four tiles: Plans work, Implements, Reviews, Tests. They write the fields the backend already selects on (delegation and the planning, implementation, review and testing capabilities), so no new role field exists. Planning is exclusive because a member cannot both delegate and receive tasks. Effort is Low, Medium or High and starts at Medium. Implemented on the Teams page on 2026-11-18. The model list is loaded from the engine only when Refresh list is pressed; in the app the dropdown is the browser's own, so "new" is text after the model name.
